title: Putting Off the Old Self
sourceBasis: World English Bible — 66-book Old and New Testament Scripture text already installed in Iron Sharpener
definition: Putting off the old self means rejecting the former patterns of sin, deception, corruption, and desire that belonged to life apart from Christ. Believers are called to lay aside what no longer fits their new life in Him.
summary: Putting off the old self means rejecting the former patterns of sin, deception, corruption, and desire that belonged to life apart from Christ. Believers are called to lay aside what no longer fits their new life in Him.
christFocus: Jesus Christ frees His people from the dominion of the old life. Because believers are joined to His death and resurrection, they are called to turn away from the sinful ways they once walked in.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
The old self describes the life shaped by sin before Christ. It includes corrupt desires, deceitful patterns, sinful habits, destructive speech, bitterness, impurity, pride, and unbelief.

Putting off the old self is not pretending the old patterns no longer tempt believers. It is actively rejecting what belongs to the former life because Christ has made His people new.

This doctrine is closely connected to repentance. Believers lay aside sin not to become their own saviors, but because the old life no longer has the right to rule those who belong to Jesus.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content:
Some believers try to add Christianity on top of old patterns without actually turning from them. Scripture does not call for decorating the old self with religious language; it calls for putting it off.

This doctrine gives clarity to the fight against sin. Grace does not leave the old life in charge.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Ask God to show you what belongs to the old self. Name sinful patterns honestly, reject excuses, and lay aside what hinders obedience. Replace secrecy with confession, passivity with repentance, and self-trust with dependence on Christ.
